neighbours.label: Fires on mid-sentence words in food, cooking and restaurant-review text, where a dish or food word is about to come (e.g. 'my favorite', 'I made', 'try the', 'went great with'); quiet in non-food text using the same phrasings
fire: After a long hike we finally sat down at the little diner, and my husband said he would try the smoked brisket while I ordered the lemon tart.
Grandma always said that whatever you stir into the pot first decides how the whole stew will taste, so I made her recipe with extra onions and browned them slowly.
The review was glowing: the crust on the pizza was blistered and chewy, and the house red went great with the wild mushroom pie.
Here are a few of my favorite weeknight dinners, all of which come together in under thirty minutes with a single skillet.
We were craving something warm after the storm, so we stopped at a roadside stand famous for its fried catfish and sweet tea.

Dessert arrived last; the waiter set down a bowl of warm bread pudding drizzled with caramel and a scoop of vanilla ice cream on the side.

short: Food-talk context before a dish word
notes: 10x pilot (concept-maps/tenx, census arm): label and 16 sentences written by a fresh Sonnet 5.5 subagent from a packet (card + all-pole band samples + concept-census evidence (which concepts and domains selected the pole)); no probes. An Opus gate checked rule-level items only (8 + 8, 0 overlap with census and probe text, near misses free of the declared trigger) and edited nothing. Labeller's note: Strong activations land on many different tokens (made, love, favorite, commas, 'in', 'rock') but always inside food, recipe or restaurant-review prose, and the output suppresses food words, so it looks like a 'a food word is coming' context pole rather than a token; census shows 72% of foods hit but no everyday objects. Coverage is uncertain since the pole is sparse and the exact token within the passage is variable.
